scopeReview: SPS-7.B.1/B.2: five activity sectors, broad employment structure, labor/transport/resources/markets, intermodal transfer and containers, least-cost reasoning and relational production patterns.
varietyReview: Four assessed original stimuli: three-site cost account, two-location weight-loss model, sector-share chart and ship/rail transfer map. Other applications distinguish activities, knowledge/leadership functions, source orientation, containerization and clustering.
repetitionReview: Numeric tasks separate total private cost and tonne-km mass change. Sector and intermodal tasks require different evidence. Avoids reducing country roles to one wage or claiming all modern locations follow Weber. Varied keys and all-option explanations; difficulty uncalibrated.
referenceNote: Official curriculum and authored academic explanation of least transport cost/labor/agglomeration checked. Original figures and assumptions only; no borrowed questions, new student resource or independent human review.

questions.independentReview: Independent totals120/115/110,unique minimumC. Savings are positive amounts explicitly subtracted, not added; no hidden negative costs or unrelated site recommendation.

questions.correctOption: The source option costs 200 units and the market option 600, favoring the source by 400.
questions.independentReview: Independently recomputed tonne-km costs200/600 anddifference400. One source, one market, no local movement charge, equal rate and all other costs equal; options limited to S/M, no unstated intermediate optimum.

questions.correctOption: B has a 40-percentage-point higher service share than A.
questions.independentReview: Verified totals100 forboth[60,25,15]/[15,30,55] andservicegap40points. Services include higher-order service functions here; categories are not counted twice.

questions.correctOption: Cargo transfers between transport modes at the port.
questions.independentReview: NodeP is sharedendpointofship andrail routes; F is inlanddestination. Does not equate containerization with no handling or imply break-of-bulk requires opening every container.

questions.correctOption: Mining ore; making steel; providing freight transport.
questions.independentReview: Activity-based classification avoids firm-name confusion or treating transport of physical goods as manufacturing.

questions.correctOption: Specialized information work can be quaternary; top-level decision-making can be quinary.
questions.independentReview: Acknowledges grouping conventions vary and higher-order services nested in broad services; no double counting or universal occupational-rank claim.

questions.correctOption: Processing near the source can avoid shipping material that will not remain in the finished product.
questions.independentReview: Conceptual extension of the numeric two-option model without introducing an unverified real material ratio; one answer defensible under conditional wording.

questions.correctOption: It can reduce some transfer time and handling costs while retaining the need for intermodal facilities.
questions.independentReview: No fixed numerical cost saving or claim containers eliminate transshipment. Matches explicit shipping-container location scope.

questions.correctOption: Clustering benefits can offset some higher location costs.
questions.independentReview: Uses agglomeration as one of least-cost adjustments with conditional advantages; preserves distinction from economies of scale within one firm.

questions.correctOption: The model may omit institutions, risk, service reliability, environmental constraints and strategic market decisions.
questions.independentReview: Rejects universal model fit without claiming cost factors no longer matter. No real business location recommendation.
